selection_goal: Show Wrench at its intended bounded strengths with one internal product-value scorecard and four public external benchmarks: paired workflow impact (CodeScaleBench), context quality (ContextBench), repository exploration (SWE-Explore-Bench), and fixed-budget retrieval/selective behavior (Agent Retrieval Bench V2). Each has a public evaluator and published outside-model or outside-system references. Published rows are reference-only; direct outside-model claims require matched cases, interface, budget, and evaluator. The slate was selected before results and weak or negative Wrench scores remain visible.

comparison_rules: Use the exact public task release, evaluator, case IDs, and fixed budgets for Wrench and outside baselines before claiming a direct comparison.
Published leaderboard scores from a different split, prompt, harness, or downstream agent are reference-only.
Preserve the Wrench verifier, six-action allowlist, read-only exploration boundary, and review-only patch boundary.
Keep retrieval-only quality distinct from downstream issue success, and keep component results distinct from the internal three-arm product replay.
Do not train or tune on public test splits or the sealed Wrench final split.
Record exact model, tokenizer, head, quantization, dataset, evaluator, and harness hashes with every run.
Keep at least 10% host RAM and 10% VRAM free during all evaluation runs.
Retain and report prior negative or poorly matched diagnostics; do not hide or replace their results when adding the new selected slate.
Choose suites by Wrench authority and metric fit before seeing Wrench results; report every selected benchmark, including negative results, without post-score substitution.
selection_guard: Prioritize benchmark-task fit to Wrench read-only retrieval, context value, and paired tool impact.
